1.w: Dead flies rising up [in] the ointment of a perfumer give a stench; a little folly is heavier than wisdom and honor.

2.w: The heart of a wise one [is] to his right, and the heart of a fool to his left.

3.w: And even in a fool walking along the way, his heart is lacking, and he shows to everyone [that] he [is] a fool.

4.w: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, you should not leave your station, for calmness puts to rest great sins.

5.w: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, as an error that goes forth from before the face of the ruler:

6.w: He has set a fool in many high places, and the rich ones sit in the lowly place.

7.w: I have seen slaves on horses, and princes walking like slaves on the earth.

8.w: The one digging a pit will fall into it; and one breaking through a wall, a snake will bite him.

9.w: The one pulling out stones will be hurt by them; the one splitting trees endangers himself by them.

10.w: If the iron has been blunt, and he has not sharpened the edge, then he must exert strength; and wisdom [is] an advantage to being successful.

11.w: If the snake bites without a charm, then there is no advantage for the master of the tongue.

12.w: The words of the mouth of a wise one [are] favor, and the lips of a fool will swallow him up—

13.w: the beginning of the words of his mouth [is] folly, and the end of his mouth [is] evil madness.

14.w: And the fool multiplies words. Man does not know what will come to be, and of what will come to be after him, who can declare [it] to him?

15.w: The toil of fools wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.

16.w: Woe to you, O land, that your king is a youth, and your princes feast in the morning!

17.w: Blessed [are] you, O land, that your king [is] a son of nobles, and your princes feast in due season—for strength and not for drunkenness!

18.w: By laziness, the rafter is made to sink, and by idleness of hands, the house leaks.

19.w: Bread is made for laughter, and wine makes life merry—and the silver is the answer to all.

20.w: Even in your thought you must not belittle the king, and in the chambers of your bed do not belittle the rich, for a bird of the heavens may carry along your voice, and a possessor of wings may declare the word.
